ShortDescription.Value: A better vanilla building menu: sorting, categories, filters and more details.

Publish.LongDescription:
A better version of the vanilla building menu, with sorting, categories and more details. Click any toolbar menu (Roads, Electricity, Education, Zones and the rest) and you get a panel instead of the row of icons.
* Grid, list, cards or table. Category tabs and a search box. * Sort by cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot, level or parking. * Group by type, theme, source, density, footprint, cost or progression. * Filter by unlocked, DLC, theme, asset pack, placement, role or source. Density has its own tabs. * Set a range for cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot width or lot depth. * Hover an asset to see its numbers and what unlocks it. * Building upgrades get names, cost and footprint too.
The list holds what the menu holds. Trees are under Landscaping; props, decals and hidden assets are not, and there is no object picker. Use Find It for those.
Works with Find It and does not replace it. Find It is a window over every asset in the game; this mod changes the toolbar menus. When Find It's window is open it takes the menu slot; this panel returns when it closes.
No Harmony patches, nothing saved to your city. Remove it any time.
**Options** (Options > Better Building Menu): switch back to the stock icon row; tile size; widen searches to every menu automatically.
Bugs and requests: the comments on this page.
Forked from Find It 1.5.8 by T. D. W. Thanks also to YenYang (UI), Algernon, Chameleon (icons) and Baka-gourd (focus handling).
This mod was developed with AI assistance (Anthropic's Claude), under human direction and review.
Publish.ChangeLog:
0.3.0
Changes * The build menu opens where the game's own does, at its size. Pick one of five Widths under Options › Better Building Menu, or drag the menu's right edge to one; every menu opens at it. * If you used an earlier version, the menu opens at the width nearest the one you had. * At the wider Widths, the tool options move to the left edge of the screen to make room for the menu. * The search, Sort, Filter, Group, View and close sit along the menu's top edge. Each control opens its own list, and a click elsewhere closes it. View also offers Width and More options…. * The search box names the building Enter will place, or says All matches locked. * The control pane is now the option Control pane: off for new players, as you had it if you used an earlier version. * The pane's Reset menu is gone: Options › Better Building Menu › Reset the build menu… puts the menu back. * Pick the sort that is already chosen to reverse it. In Group, Category is now By tab and None is now No groups. * While a terraforming brush is in hand, the menu stays open and keeps answering your search and filters, as the game's own menu does. * Enter in the search arms the best match, wherever it sits in the list and however the list is sorted. * A sort's first click puts the best first, the most of a capacity or the lowest Cost or Upkeep; ties go to the cheaper building. * Sort by Households, Water capacity or Sewage capacity. * Options › Better Building Menu › Reset the build menu… puts the options, the menu's size and each menu's View and Group back, after asking. * While Replace the vanilla build menu is off, the other options are greyed out and say why. * With a controller, the game's own build menu shows. Move the mouse and this menu comes back, on the same menu. * The menu's tabs sit along its bottom edge, next to the toolbar: All with the menu's icon, then each tab's icon over its count. The counts follow your filters and your search, and a tab they empty stays in its place. * At the right end of the tabs, the tab you are on sits over how many buildings the list holds of how many match. The end of the list shows only the button that loads more. * Education's school levels are named chips beside the Education tab. * A menu opens on the tab of the building you last picked from it, with that building at the top of the list; with nothing picked, on its first tab, and Education on its first school level. A menu in Cards, or with few buildings, opens on All. Opening a menu clears the search. * Picking a sort, or clicking the tab that is already lit, takes the list back to its top. Going back to that building's tab brings it back to the top. * While you type in the search box, Up and Down change the building Enter places, marked ↵ in the list, and Page Up and Page Down scroll the list. Esc closes an open list, then clears the search, then closes the menu. * The search box lets go of the arrow keys after Enter, picking a building or closing the menu, so they move the camera again. It shows an outline while you are typing in it. * On a wider menu, each tab shows its name beside its icon when they all fit. * A small mark under the menu points to its toolbar button. * The menu follows the game's Interface style and Interface transparency. * Each menu remembers its own View: List, Tiles or Cards. Options › Default view sets what each menu draws until you pick its View; it starts at Auto. Auto draws a list for most menus and tiles for zones and prop catalogues. Grid is now Tiles, Table is now List. * If you used an earlier version, Default view starts at your View: Grid as Tiles, Table as List. * List puts each building on a plate with its picture, name and cost, 20 a screen, more columns when wider. Above 100% text, Options › At large text picks More buildings or Whole names. * Tiles shows pictures with their cost, and names the one you point at. Options › Tile size is set to 64, once; a size you pick after that stays. * A tile's tag shows a long cost in thousands or millions, and under a sort by a number, that number. * List, Tiles and Cards say MS n while the city waits on that milestone, else Locked, and keep the unique and built marks. * Each menu remembers its Group, and its Sort until you quit. * Typing searches the whole menu, best match first, and Sort reads Match. Clearing it brings back your tab and sort. * Cards are the cards of earlier versions, three rows to the menu's height, each as wide as its name. * In All, the list, tiles and cards name each tab with its count. A tab mostly locked lists what you can build first, then Locked: click it to fold the locked ones away. * A menu with few buildings shows them bigger in the list. * At a wider Width, search results fill the columns under the search box first.
Fixed * A list that stops at 2,000 buildings says so, and how to narrow it. * Under Metric filters, a min or max that is not a number is outlined in red.
